53.0.s.en: 1. The Cross is a transcendent mystery:

53.0.0.en: 1 Who hath believed our report? and to whom is the arm of the LORD revealed?

53.0.1.en: The prophet opens his discourse on the Cross, saying: “Who hath believed our report? and to whom is the arm of the LORD revealed?” [1].

53.0.2.en: If the contemporaries of the prophet Isaiah were unable to accept the prophecies concerning the appearing of Cyrus to bring the people back from the Babylonian captivity, how could they believe the matter of the Cross?! Truly it is a wondrous mystery before which the heavenly and the earthly stand in amazement, as they see the arm of the Lord revealed through the Incarnation, so that the Lord might stretch out His hands on the Cross to embrace the Gentiles, granting them the power of His resurrection and its joy through their fellowship in His sufferings and His crucifixion.

53.0.3.en: * That God, the Son of God, the arm of the Lord, should endure such sufferings!

53.0.4.en: St. Cyril of Jerusalem The subject of the revealing of the arm of the Lord, or the incarnation of the Word of God, remains a subject of amazement for the heavenly and earthly creation: how does the Word become flesh?!

53.0.5.en: * With what words shall we bless God, and what thanks can we offer Him...?!

53.0.6.en: He loved us so much that, though He is the Eternal One, older than the whole world itself, He became in age younger than many of His servants in the world!

53.0.7.en: Like a child He cried in speechless infancy, He who is the “Word” without whom all the eloquence of men is unable to speak!

53.0.8.en: Behold, O man, what God became for your sake...?!

53.0.9.en: Though you were a man, you wished to be God and went astray! And He, though He is God, wished to be man in order to bring back the one who had gone astray!

53.0.10.en: Human pride brought you down, so that only by divine humility might you be raised up!

53.0.11.en: St. Augustine * No one has been able to speak of Your eternity, so let me speak of Your coming, O my Teacher, with amazement...

53.0.12.en: Love drew You to come to our country for our sake... You became with us and of us, and You are our Lord!

53.0.13.en: Behold, Immanuel is with us, beside us, and for this reason tongues unworthy of You have spoken...

53.0.14.en: St. James of Serugh By saying “and to whom is the arm of the LORD revealed?!” [1] he means the appearing of the Lord Christ, not only in history, which amazes the whole creation, but also His appearing in our personal life, or His continual manifestation in the heart as a source of inner satisfaction.

53.0.15.en: * The arm of the Lord is Christ, so do not forget Him! Do not let (the spiritual enemies) rejoice, saying: Christians exist only for a time!

53.0.16.en: * “And to whom is the arm of the LORD revealed?!”

53.0.17.en: By giving you His Christ He gives you His arm, and by giving you His arm He gives you His Christ.

53.0.18.en: He leads (man) to the way by leading him to His Christ, and He leads him to His Christ by leading him to the way, and Christ is the truth.

53.0.19.en: * “Thou openest thine hand, they are filled with good” (Ps 104:28).

53.0.20.en: What does it mean, O Lord, that You open Your hand? Christ is Your hand. “To whom is the arm of the LORD revealed?!” It is opened when it is revealed, for revelation is an opening. “Thou openest thine hand, they are filled with good”; when You reveal Your Christ, they are filled with good.

53.0.21.en: St. Augustine Our Christ, the arm of the Father, has been revealed to us that we may enjoy Him as the mystery of our life, saying: “For the life was manifested, and we have seen it, and bear witness, and shew unto you that eternal life, which was with the Father, and was manifested unto us” (1 Jn 1:2).

53.1.s.en: 2. The Cross is shame and disgrace:

53.1.0.en: 2 For he shall grow up before him as a tender plant, and as a root out of a dry ground: he hath no form nor comeliness; and when we shall see him, there is no beauty that we should desire him. 3 He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief: and we hid as it were our faces from him; he was despised, and we esteemed him not.

53.1.1.en: The Lord, the Savior, came like a branch growing up before Israel and like a root out of a dry ground; therefore the people made light of Him, and His own received Him not.

53.1.2.en: “He shall grow up before him as a tender plant” [2], for He came from the seed of David as a small shoot, as a branch, though He is the Creator of the vine and the One who brought it into being. He came hidden, in humility, and so He was symbolized by the bush burning with fire, which appears a weak plant with no strength, yet in His divinity He is a blazing fire!

53.1.3.en: He came “before” Israel as the Shepherd who goes ahead of His flock!

53.1.4.en: “And as a root out of a dry ground” [2]; His appearing came in an unexpected way, for the Jews thought they would see the Messiah as a great king with authority, able to shatter the Roman Empire and to establish a state that would rule the world; but He came as a hidden root in dry ground, from which no one expects that it will sprout and bear fruit. He came from a dry ground, for He was born of St. Mary, who was betrothed to Joseph the carpenter, and both of them were poor; “though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, that ye through his poverty might be rich” (2 Cor 8:9).

53.1.5.en: The Lord Christ came as a root out of a dry ground, for the Jews at that time were in a state of severe dryness; He came in the midst of the dryness to make a paradise out of the wilderness. The bride said of Him: “As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons” (Song 2:3).

53.1.6.en: “He hath no form nor comeliness; and when we shall see him, there is no beauty that we should desire him. He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief: and we hid as it were our faces from him; he was despised, and we esteemed him not” [2-3].

53.1.7.en: Here the prophet moves from the scene of the Incarnation to the scene of the Cross. In the Incarnation he saw Him as a small shoot from the seed of David, and a root out of a dry ground; He came as a son of men when all humanity, including the people of God, was in complete dryness, and He came from a poor family, so that Nathanael said: Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth?! Now the prophet looks upon the scene of the Cross and sees it without form, without comeliness, without appearance, despised, so that no one dares to approach it, a man of sorrows, from whose sight we hide and cover our faces because of the intense grief.

53.1.8.en: * He has no form nor comeliness in the eyes of the Jews, but to David He is fairer than the children of men (Ps 45:2). On the mountain (at the Transfiguration) He was radiant and shone more than the sun (Mt 17:2), pointing us to His future mystery.

53.1.9.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus * He who is fairer than the children of men was seen by men on the Cross without form or comeliness; His face was bowed down, and His position unseemly. Yet this lack of comeliness in your Savior poured out the price of your inner beauty, for the glory of the king’s son is from within (Ps 45:2).

53.2.s.en: 3. The Cross is redemption and salvation:

53.2.0.en: 4 Surely he hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows: yet we did esteem him stricken, smitten of God, and afflicted. 5 But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed. 6 All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way; and the LORD hath laid on him the iniquity of us all. 7 He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he opened not his mouth: he is brought as a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is dumb, so he openeth not his mouth. 8 He was taken from prison and from judgment: and who shall declare his generation? for he was cut off out of the land of the living: for the transgression of my people was he stricken. 9 And he made his grave with the wicked, and with the rich in his death; because he had done no violence, neither was any deceit in his mouth. 10 Yet it pleased the LORD to bruise him; he hath put him to grief: when thou shalt make his soul an offering for sin, he shall see his seed, he shall prolong his days, and the pleasure of the LORD shall prosper in his hand. 11 He shall see of the travail of his soul, and shall be satisfied: by his knowledge shall my righteous servant justify many; for he shall bear their iniquities. 12 Therefore will I divide him a portion with the great, and he shall divide the spoil with the strong; because he hath poured out his soul unto death: and he was numbered with the transgressors; and he bare the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors.

53.2.1.en: After speaking of the Cross from the outside, he leads us into its depths that we may discover its mystery and its power as a sin offering and an atonement for our sins, saying:

53.2.2.en: “Surely he hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows: yet we did esteem him stricken, smitten of God, and afflicted” [4]. What He bore was not His own griefs nor His own sorrows, but our griefs and our cares and our wounds...

53.2.3.en: What He bears is the weight of our sins, which He willingly bowed down to carry in His body for us, out of His love.

53.2.4.en: * He bore our sins and carried our diseases, and yet He suffered nothing that needed a cure, for He was tempted in all things like as we are, yet without sin. He who persecutes the light that shines in the darkness cannot overcome it.

53.2.5.en: * He was bruised and wounded, yet He healed every disease and every weakness.

53.2.6.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus * Be not ashamed of the Crucified One, but rather boast of Him, saying: He bore our sins, He carried our sorrows, and with His stripes we are healed.

53.2.7.en: St. Cyril of Jerusalem The Lord Christ bore our sorrows, as we saw Him in the Garden of Gethsemane drinking our cup to the end, in all its bitterness, when He prayed to His Father, saying: “O my Father, if this cup may not pass away from me, except I drink it, thy will be done” (Mt 26:42). He took Peter and the two sons of Zebedee so that they might see Him begin to be sorrowful and very heavy, saying to them: “My soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death” (Mt 26:38).

53.3.0.en: “For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin” (2 Cor 5:21), for He offered Himself as a sin offering, bearing our sins and our iniquities and making atonement for them. “But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him [had He not endured the chastisement for us, we would not have enjoyed peace]; and with his stripes we are healed. All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way; and the LORD hath laid on him the iniquity of us all” [5-6].

53.3.1.en: * The Lord delivered His body to death that we might be sanctified through the forgiveness of sins, which is accomplished by the sprinkling of His blood...

53.3.2.en: We must thank the Lord from the depths, for He told us of the things that are past, and gave us wisdom concerning the things that are present, and did not leave us without understanding concerning the things to come.

53.3.3.en: The Epistle of Barnabas * We are cleansed by His precious blood, which purifies us from every sin, His blood which does not cry out for vengeance like the blood of Abel (Heb 12:24).

53.3.4.en: Pope Athanasius the Apostolic * Let us remind ourselves of the benefit of the true faith. For it is useful for me to know that Christ bore my weaknesses for me, and submitted to the sufferings of my body; so that for my sake, that is, for the sake of each one, He became sin and a curse (2 Cor 5:21; Gal 3:13).

53.3.5.en: For my sake He humbled Himself and submitted...!

53.3.6.en: He became a curse, not in respect of His divinity but in respect of His humanity, for it is written: “Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree” (Gal 3:13).

53.3.7.en: In the flesh He was hanged, and therefore He became a curse, He who bore our curse!

53.3.8.en: He wept so that you, O man, would not weep much!

53.3.9.en: What a glorious remedy! That we should have the consolation of Christ.

53.3.10.en: He endured these things with wondrous patience for our sake... and we truly cannot endure ordinary patience for His name’s sake.

53.3.11.en: Behold, His tears wash us and His weeping cleanses us!

53.3.12.en: St. Ambrose * By death He raised the dead from death, for He bore the curse, saving us from it.

53.3.13.en: St. John Chrysostom * By the death of the Righteous One, which was accomplished of His own free choice, He removed the death of sinners, which occurred of necessity as a judgment we deserve.

53.4.0.en: St. Augustine “He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he opened not his mouth: he is brought as a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is dumb, so he openeth not his mouth” [7].

53.4.1.en: The prophet speaks here in the past tense, and as St. John Chrysostom says: [This was the custom of the prophets of old, to speak of the future as of the past].

53.4.2.en: * Surely the prophecy speaks most plainly of the Lord Jesus when it is said, “as a lamb to the slaughter” [7] (as being our Passover).

53.4.3.en: Your forehead has been anointed with the sign (of His blood) and also the doorposts, since all Christians bear the same sign.

53.4.4.en: St. Augustine * When (Pilate and the religious leaders) entered into dialogue with one another, He was in peace, fulfilling the saying of the prophet: “He opened not his mouth; in his humiliation his judgment was taken away” [7-8] (the Septuagint).

53.4.5.en: St. John Chrysostom * It was fitting for Him to be silent during His sufferings, but He will not be silent in the judgment.

53.4.6.en: He who afterwards comes as Judge came to be judged; therefore He will come with authority to judge, He who in great humility was judged.

53.4.7.en: * He bore evil patiently, since He would afterwards bring righteousness.

53.4.8.en: * When He was led as a sacrifice, “before her shearers he opened not his mouth,” and when He was crucified and buried He was always the hidden God of gods.

53.4.9.en: St. Augustine * When He was scourged, He was silent! And when He was crucified, He prayed for those who crucified Him! “What shall I render unto the LORD for all his benefits toward me? I will take the cup of salvation, and call upon the name of the LORD” (Ps 116:12-13).

53.4.10.en: St. Jerome St. Augustine sees that the Lord Christ was silent during His trial and mockery because He hid His divinity so that they might accomplish what they wanted; but in His final coming to judge, “he doth send out his voice, and that a mighty voice” (Ps 68:33), “shall not keep silence” (Ps 50:3), for He reveals His divinity.

53.5.0.en: “And who shall declare his generation? for he was cut off out of the land of the living: for the transgression of my people was he stricken” [8].

53.5.1.en: * “Who shall declare his generation?” [8]. He was born eternally... He was born of the Father without time, and He was born of the Virgin in the fullness of times.

53.6.0.en: St. Augustine “And he made his grave with the wicked, and with the rich in his death; because he had done no violence, neither was any deceit in his mouth” [9].

53.6.1.en: * They crucified Him with thieves, fulfilling the prophecy involuntarily. What they did to dishonor Him was counted for truth, that you may perceive the great power of the prophecy...

53.6.2.en: Satan tried to throw a veil over what happened but he failed, because the three were crucified, yet Jesus alone was glorified, that we may perceive His authority over all. Miracles took place when the three were nailed to the crosses, but no one ascribed what happened to the other two, but to Jesus alone. Thus the plan of Satan was completely frustrated and everything turned back upon his own head, for one of the two thieves was saved, one who did not offend against the glory of the Cross but contributed to it not a little. For the changing of a thief while on the cross and drawing him into Paradise is no less than the shaking of the rocks.

53.6.3.en: St. John Chrysostom St. Augustine sees that the prophecy “And he made his grave with the wicked” was fulfilled by the setting of wicked guards at the tomb of the Lord Christ, who accepted a bribe to lie, saying, “His disciples came by night, and stole him away while we slept” (Mt 28:13). They spoke falsely and so bore witness to His resurrection, for if they were asleep, how did they know that His disciples stole Him?! They testified that His body was not in the tomb, while their accusation of the theft of the body is a matter that reason does not accept.

53.7.0.en: “Because he hath poured out his soul unto death: and he was numbered with the transgressors; and he bare the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors” [12].

53.7.1.en: * If for your sake and for the sake of your sins He was numbered with the transgressors, then be a keeper of the Law for His sake. Worship Him who was hanged for your sake, even if you yourself are hanged... Buy your salvation with your death, and enter with Jesus into Paradise, that you may know from whence you are fallen (Rev 2:5).

53.7.2.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus * He intercedes for us every day, washing our feet, and we too need to have our feet washed daily by walking in truth with spiritual steps, so that we may know the Lord’s Prayer, saying:

53.7.3.en: “And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors” (Mt 6:12).
